20:  * GPIO2/GPIO3/GPIO4/GPIO5, which per the chip's pinmux table
21:  * (bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h GPIO_DEV_MAP)
22:  * carry QSPI1_CLK/QSPI1_CSN/QSPI1_IO0/QSPI1_IO1 (function-select index 6),

49:  *   cmd_d_h     0x54 (REG_0x15)
50:  *   cmd_d_cfg1  0x58 (REG_0x16)
51:  *   cmd_d_cfg2  0x5c (REG_0x17) - bit[0] cmd_start
52:  *   status      0x70 (REG_0x1c) - bit[2] cmd_start_done
53:  *   status_clr  0x6c (REG_0x1b) - bit[2] clr_cmd_start_done
54:  *
55:  * The "command done" flag is carried by the status register's
56:  * cmd_start_done bit, not by core_status (REG_0x03, byte offset 0x0c),
57:  * which is an unused, un-bitfielded raw word in the vendor headers and is
58:  * never read by qspi_ll_is_cmd_start_done()/qspi_ll_wait_cmd_done().  The
59:  * start trigger is not a separate register either: it is the cmd_start bit
60:  * inside each channel's own cfg2 register (cmd_c_cfg2 for the send path,
61:  * cmd_d_cfg2 for the read path), matching qspi_ll_cmd_c_start() and
62:  * qspi_ll_cmd_d_start().
63:  *
64:  * Pinmux: the QSPI1 controller's four signal lines (CLK/CSN/IO0/IO1) are
65:  * shared, multiplexed GPIO pads (GPIO_2/3/4/5 on this SoC), not dedicated
66:  * pins.  Each pad defaults to plain GPIO after reset and must be switched
67:  * to QSPI1 mode via the "second function" pinmux mechanism before the
68:  * controller's TX/RX lines are actually connected to the pad -- without
69:  * this step cmd_start_done never asserts because the panel never receives
70:  * the command.  Source of the function-select index (6) for QSPI1 on
71:  * GPIO_2/3/4/5: bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
72:  * ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h gpio_map_table (QSPI1_CLK/
73:  * CSN/IO0/IO1 are the 7th entry, index 6, in each pin's per-function
74:  * array).  The pinmux register plumbing itself (BK7258_GPIO_SYS_BASE etc.)
75:  * is shared with bk7258_gpio.c; see bk7258_gpio_set_function().
76:  *
77:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
78:  ****************************************************************************/
79: 
80: #include <nuttx/config.h>
81: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
82: #include <stdbool.h>
83: #include <stdint.h>
84: 
85: #include "arm_internal.h"
86: #include "hardware/bk7258_memorymap.h"
87: #include "hardware/bk7258_sysctrl.h"
88: #include "bk7258_gpio.h"
89: #include "bk7258_qspi.h"
90: 
91: #define QSPI1_CLK_PIN               2u
92: #define QSPI1_CSN_PIN               3u
93: #define QSPI1_IO0_PIN               4u
94: #define QSPI1_IO1_PIN               5u
95: #define QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION       6u
96: 
97: #define QSPI_REG(offset)           (BK7258_QSPI1_BASE + (offset))
98: 
99: #define QSPI_GLB_CTRL              QSPI_REG(0x08u)
100: #define QSPI_GLB_CTRL_SOFT_RESET   (1u << 0)
101: 
102: #define QSPI_CMD_C_L               QSPI_REG(0x40u)
103: #define QSPI_CMD_C_H               QSPI_REG(0x44u)
104: #define QSPI_CMD_C_CFG1            QSPI_REG(0x48u)
105: #define QSPI_CMD_C_CFG2            QSPI_REG(0x4cu)
106: 
107: #define QSPI_CMD_D_L               QSPI_REG(0x50u)
108: #define QSPI_CMD_D_H               QSPI_REG(0x54u)
109: #define QSPI_CMD_D_CFG1            QSPI_REG(0x58u)
110: #define QSPI_CMD_D_CFG2            QSPI_REG(0x5cu)
111: 
112: #define QSPI_STATUS                QSPI_REG(0x70u)
113: #define QSPI_STATUS_CMD_START_DONE (1u << 2)
114: 
115: #define QSPI_STATUS_CLR                 QSPI_REG(0x6cu)
116: #define QSPI_STATUS_CLR_CMD_START_DONE  (1u << 2)
117: 
118: #define QSPI_CMD_START_BIT         (1u << 0)
119: 
120: /* Matches qspi_ll_wait_cmd_done()'s 10000-iteration bound
121:  * (ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/qspi_ll.h) instead of looping forever,
122:  * so a pinmux or wiring problem produces a diagnosable timeout rather than
123:  * an unrecoverable hang. */
124: #define QSPI_WAIT_DONE_MAX_ITER    10000
125: 
126: static bool bk7258_qspi0_wait_done(void)
127: {
128:   int i;
129: 
130:   for (i = 0; i < QSPI_WAIT_DONE_MAX_ITER; i++)
131:     {
132:       if ((getreg32(QSPI_STATUS) & QSPI_STATUS_CMD_START_DONE) != 0)
133:         {
134:           break;
135:         }
136: 
137:       up_udelay(1);
138:     }
139: 
140:   /* Clear cmd_start_done (write 1 then 0), matching qspi_ll_wait_cmd_done()
141:    * -- required so a stale "done" flag from this command does not make
142:    * the next command's wait loop return immediately without having
143:    * actually completed. */
144:   modifyreg32(QSPI_STATUS_CLR, 0, QSPI_STATUS_CLR_CMD_START_DONE);
145:   modifyreg32(QSPI_STATUS_CLR, QSPI_STATUS_CLR_CMD_START_DONE, 0);
146: 
147:   return i < QSPI_WAIT_DONE_MAX_ITER;
148: }
149: 
150: void bk7258_qspi0_init(void)
151: {
152:   /* Enable the QSPI1 *module* clock gate first, matching
153:    * qspi_id_init_common()'s documented call order ("1. set clock, 2. set
154:    * gpio as qspi, 3. enable interrupt") in bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
155:    * ap/middleware/driver/qspi/qspi_driver.c.  Without this bit, register
156:    * writes to the QSPI1 block are accepted (no bus fault) but the
157:    * controller's internal command state machine has no clock to run on,
158:    * so cmd_start_done never asserts -- see
159:    * hardware/bk7258_sysctrl.h's BK7258_QSPI1_MODULE_CLK_EN comment for
160:    * the register-map citation and the I2C1 precedent this is modeled
161:    * after. */
162:   modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_DEVCLK_EN, 0, BK7258_QSPI1_MODULE_CLK_EN);
163: 
164:   /* Switch the 4 shared GPIO pads to QSPI1 mode before touching the
165:    * controller; see file header comment for why this is required and why
166:    * it is QSPI1 (GPIO2-5) rather than QSPI0 (GPIO22-25) on this board. */
167:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(QSPI1_CLK_PIN, QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
168:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(QSPI1_CSN_PIN, QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
169:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(QSPI1_IO0_PIN, QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
170:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(QSPI1_IO1_PIN, QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
171: 
172:   putreg32(QSPI_GLB_CTRL_SOFT_RESET, QSPI_GLB_CTRL);
173:   up_udelay(10);
174:   putreg32(0, QSPI_GLB_CTRL);
175: }
176: 
177: bool bk7258_qspi0_send_cmd(uint8_t cmd, const uint8_t *data, uint8_t data_len)
178: {
179:   uint32_t cmd_c_h = (uint32_t)cmd;
180:   uint32_t cmd_c_l = 0;
181:   uint8_t i;
182: 
183:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_C_L);
184:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_C_H);
185:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_C_CFG1);
186:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_C_CFG2);
187: 
188:   if (data_len > 0 && data_len <= 4)
189:     {
190:       for (i = 0; i < data_len; i++)
191:         {
192:           cmd_c_l |= ((uint32_t)data[i]) << (i * 8);
193:         }
194: 
195:       putreg32(cmd_c_l, QSPI_CMD_C_L);
196:     }
197: 
198:   putreg32(cmd_c_h, QSPI_CMD_C_H);
199:   modifyreg32(QSPI_CMD_C_CFG2, 0, QSPI_CMD_START_BIT);
200:   return bk7258_qspi0_wait_done();
201: }
202: 
203: uint32_t bk7258_qspi0_read_id(void)
204: {
205:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_D_L);
206:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_D_H);
207:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_D_CFG1);
208:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_D_CFG2);
209: 
210:   putreg32(0x04u, QSPI_CMD_D_H); /* GC9D01 read-ID opcode, single byte cmd */
211:   modifyreg32(QSPI_CMD_D_CFG2, 0, QSPI_CMD_START_BIT);
212:   (void)bk7258_qspi0_wait_done();
213: 
214:   return getreg32(QSPI_CMD_D_L);
215: }

1: /****************************************************************************

3:  *
4:  * GC9D01 160x160 QSPI LCD panel bring-up.  Init command table copied from
5:  * bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
6:  * ap/components/bk_peripheral/src/lcd/spi/lcd_spi_gc9d01.c (gc9d01_init_cmds,
7:  * 50 entries total).  Only the init sequence is ported; DMA-backed
8:  * full-frame refresh is out of scope for this task.
9:  *
10:  * Command table traceability: bk7258_qspi0_send_cmd() only supports up to
11:  * 4 data bytes per command (see bk7258_qspi.h), which hard-blocks porting
12:  * 11 of the 50 upstream entries whose data_len exceeds 4:
13:  *   0x74(7) 0x64(6) 0x65(6) 0x6C(7) 0x6E(32) 0x70(6) 0xF0(6) 0xF2(6)
14:  *   0xF1(6) 0xF3(6), plus the special 0x00/data_len=0xFF delay marker
15:  *   (handled separately below, not a real QSPI command).
16:  * The remaining 9 omitted entries (0x98, 0xB5, 0x60, 0x61, 0x6A, 0x93,
17:  * 0x71, 0x91, 0x34) all fit within the 4-byte limit and were dropped in
18:  * an earlier revision of this file without a stated reason; upstream
19:  * documents them as gamma/porch/timing fine-tuning registers that are not
20:  * required to reach a functional display state, but this has not been
21:  * independently confirmed against the GC9D01 datasheet.  If the panel
22:  * shows visible artifacts once full-frame refresh is implemented, restore
23:  * these 9 entries first as they are the cheapest to re-add (all <= 4
24:  * bytes, no interface change needed).
25:  *
26:  * One functional gap from an earlier revision of this file has been
27:  * fixed here: upstream sends {0x00, {0x78}, 0xFF} between the Sleep Out
28:  * (0x11) and Display On (0x29) commands.  data_len == 0xFF is not a real
29:  * QSPI command; per bk_lcd_qspi_init() in
30:  * ap/middleware/driver/lcd/lcd_qspi_driver.c, it is a driver-level marker
31:  * meaning "delay data[0] milliseconds" (0x78 = 120ms).  This delay is
32:  * restored below as an explicit up_udelay() call between the two
33:  * commands, since bk7258_qspi0_send_cmd() has no equivalent marker
34:  * convention.
35:  *
36:  * Bus/reset-pin correction (2026-07-31): the very first init command
37:  * (0xFE) was timing out on real hardware.  Root cause was two wrong
38:  * hardware assumptions, both corrected together (diagnosed via the board
39:  * schematic, AIDK_AI玩具开发板_原理图.pdf):
40:  *   1. bk7258_qspi.c was driving QSPI0 (GPIO22-25), but this board's
41:  *      LCD is wired to QSPI1 (GPIO2-5) -- see that file's header comment
42:  *      for the full pin-by-pin schematic evidence.
43:  *   2. GC9D01_RESET_PIN below was GPIO_6 (copied from a different board's
44:  *      dual-screen reference config in BTdocs/DualScreenAVIPlayer.md);
45:  *      the schematic shows GPIO_6 floating (unconnected) on this board,
46:  *      the real LCD_RST net is GPIO45.
47:  * Neither symptom was diagnosable from register-level behavior alone
48:  * (cmd_start_done simply never asserts when the controller drives pins
49:  * the panel isn't wired to); both required cross-checking the schematic
50:  * against gpio_map.h's pinmux function tables.
51:  *
52:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
53:  ****************************************************************************/

55: #include <nuttx/config.h>
56: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
57: #include <stdbool.h>
58: #include <stdint.h>
59: #include <stdio.h>

61: #include "bk7258_gpio.h"
62: #include "bk7258_qspi.h"
63: 
64: /* GC9D01 reset pin, corrected against the actual board schematic
65:  * (AIDK_AI玩具开发板_原理图.pdf) after this driver's original QSPI0/GPIO6
66:  * assumption (ported from BTdocs/DualScreenAVIPlayer.md's lcd0 config,
67:  * a *different* board's dual-screen reference layout) caused the very
68:  * first init command (0xFE) to time out -- the panel was never wired to
69:  * the pins this driver was toggling.  The schematic (sheet 2/6 main chip
70:  * pin table) shows GPIO_6 net-labelled nothing at all on this board
71:  * (floating, no connection); the actual LCD_RST net is wired to chip pin
72:  * 65 = P45 = GPIO45 (same sheet's pin table row "P45/0CSN/B5/D2/2LRCK"),
73:  * confirmed again on sheet 5/6's CN5 single-screen connector pin 13
74:  * (labelled LCD_RST). See bk7258_qspi.c's file header for the QSPI0->
75:  * QSPI1 correction that was diagnosed alongside this one (both changes
76:  * were needed to get past the same "cmd 0xFE timed out" symptom). */

79: /* Post-Sleep-Out settle delay before Display On, per upstream
80:  * gc9d01_init_cmds entry {0x00, {0x78}, 0xFF} (0x78 = 120 decimal ms). */
81: #define GC9D01_SLEEP_OUT_DELAY_MS 120u

84: {
85:   uint8_t cmd;
86:   uint8_t data[4];

93: static const struct gc9d01_init_cmd g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out[] =
94: {
95:   { 0xFE, { 0x00 }, 0 },
96:   { 0xEF, { 0x00 }, 0 },
97:   { 0x80, { 0xFF }, 1 },
98:   { 0x81, { 0xFF }, 1 },
99:   { 0x82, { 0xFF }, 1 },
100:   { 0x83, { 0xFF }, 1 },
101:   { 0x84, { 0xFF }, 1 },
102:   { 0x85, { 0xFF }, 1 },
103:   { 0x86, { 0xFF }, 1 },
104:   { 0x87, { 0xFF }, 1 },
105:   { 0x88, { 0xFF }, 1 },
106:   { 0x89, { 0xFF }, 1 },
107:   { 0x8A, { 0xFF }, 1 },
108:   { 0x8B, { 0xFF }, 1 },
109:   { 0x8C, { 0xFF }, 1 },
110:   { 0x8D, { 0xFF }, 1 },
111:   { 0x8E, { 0xFF }, 1 },
112:   { 0x8F, { 0xFF }, 1 },
113:   { 0x3A, { 0x05 }, 1 },
114:   { 0xEC, { 0x01 }, 1 },
115:   { 0xBF, { 0x01 }, 1 },
116:   { 0xF9, { 0x40 }, 1 },
117:   { 0x9B, { 0x3B }, 1 },
118:   { 0x7E, { 0x30 }, 1 },
119:   { 0xC3, { 0x18 }, 1 },
120:   { 0xC4, { 0x18 }, 1 },
121:   { 0xC9, { 0x3C }, 1 },
122:   { 0x36, { 0x00 }, 1 },
123:   { 0x11, { 0x00 }, 0 }, /* Sleep Out */
124: };

126: #define GC9D01_PRE_SLEEP_OUT_CMD_COUNT \
127:   (sizeof(g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out) / \
128:    sizeof(g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out[0]))

130: /* Display On (0x29), sent GC9D01_SLEEP_OUT_DELAY_MS after Sleep Out. */
131: static const struct gc9d01_init_cmd g_gc9d01_display_on = { 0x29, { 0x00 }, 0 };

133: /****************************************************************************
134:  * Name: bk7258_gc9d01_hw_reset
135:  *
136:  * Description:
137:  *   Drive the GC9D01 RESET pin through a high-low-high pulse to force a
138:  *   hardware reset.  Timing: the 10ms pre/post pulse widths are a
139:  *   conservative margin (GC9D01 reset pulse width requirements are
140:  *   typically in the microsecond range; 10ms has no specific datasheet
141:  *   citation but costs nothing at bring-up time).  The final 120ms
142:  *   post-reset settle delay before issuing any command matches the
143:  *   reset-to-ready delay used across every other panel driver in the same
144:  *   bk_avdk_smp codebase (ap/components/bk_peripheral/src/lcd/rgb and .../mcu
145:  *   uniformly use rtos_delay_milliseconds(120) after hardware reset, e.g.
146:  *   lcd_st7701s.c:48, lcd_nt35512.c:859, lcd_st7789v.c:167), i.e. 120ms is
147:  *   the de-facto standard settle time for this class of display driver IC
148:  *   and is not GC9D01-specific tuning.
149:  *
150:  ****************************************************************************/
151: 
152: static void bk7258_gc9d01_hw_reset(void)
153: {
154:   bk7258_gpio_output(GC9D01_RESET_PIN, true);
155:   up_udelay(10000);
156:   bk7258_gpio_write(GC9D01_RESET_PIN, false);
157:   up_udelay(10000);
158:   bk7258_gpio_write(GC9D01_RESET_PIN, true);
159:   up_udelay(120000);
160: }

162: /****************************************************************************
163:  * Name: bk7258_gc9d01_test
164:  *
165:  * Description:
166:  *   Bring-up smoke test for the GC9D01 panel: hardware reset, QSPI0 init,
167:  *   then send the full init command sequence (pre-Sleep-Out commands,
168:  *   Sleep Out, 120ms settle delay, Display On).  There is no Read ID
169:  *   command in the upstream init table (verified: the only "0x04" bytes
170:  *   found in lcd_spi_gc9d01.c are payload data, not an RDID opcode), so
171:  *   this test cannot verify success by reading back a panel ID.  Success
172:  *   criterion is therefore "the full init sequence is sent without the
173:  *   call hanging or crashing", not a register readback match.
174:  *
175:  ****************************************************************************/

178: {
179:   size_t i;
180: 
181:   printf("gc9d01: hardware reset\n");
182:   bk7258_gc9d01_hw_reset();
183: 
184:   printf("gc9d01: qspi0 init\n");
185:   bk7258_qspi0_init();

188:          (unsigned int)GC9D01_PRE_SLEEP_OUT_CMD_COUNT);
189:   for (i = 0; i < GC9D01_PRE_SLEEP_OUT_CMD_COUNT; i++)
190:     {
191:       if (!bk7258_qspi0_send_cmd(g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out[i].cmd,
192:                                  g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out[i].data,
193:                                  g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out[i].data_len))
194:         {
195:           printf("gc9d01: qspi0 timed out waiting for cmd 0x%02x "
196:                  "(index %u) to complete, aborting init sequence\n",
197:                  g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out[i].cmd, (unsigned int)i);
198:           return -1;
199:         }
200:     }
201: 
202:   printf("gc9d01: sleep-out settle delay (%u ms)\n",
203:          GC9D01_SLEEP_OUT_DELAY_MS);

1: # GC9D01 LCD 面板初始化验证 Implementation Plan
2: 
3: > **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
4: 
5: **Goal:** 在 OpenVela BK7258 AP (CPU1) 上新增最小 GPIO 驱动 + QSPI 驱动薄移植层，完成 GC9D01
6: LCD 面板初始化序列，并通过 QSPI 读回面板 ID 寄存器验证总线通信正常，作为后续整帧刷新
7: （需要 DMA，不在本计划范围）的地基。
8: 
9: **Architecture:** 三个新增模块，均放入 `board/beken/chips/bk7258/`（芯片层）：
10: 1. `bk7258_gpio.c` — 最小 GPIO 驱动，只做 output-enable / set-high / set-low，无 pinmux
11:    框架、无中断支持，仅覆盖本计划需要的 reset 引脚控制。
12: 2. `bk7258_qspi.c` — QSPI0 控制器薄移植层，从博通 `qspi_ll.h`/`qspi_hal.c` 的结构体位域
13:    代码换算为本仓库既有的扁平寄存器宏 + `getreg32`/`putreg32` 风格（与 `bk7258_mbox0.c`
14:    一致），只实现发送命令（cmd_c 通道）和轮询完成状态，不实现 DMA 帧刷新路径。
15: 3. `bk7258_gc9d01.c` — GC9D01 面板初始化命令表（从 `dvp_gc9d01.c` 等价搬运，纯数据）+
16:    一个 NSH 可调用的测试入口函数，执行：GPIO reset 时序 → QSPI0 时钗使能 → 发送 GC9D01
17:    60 条初始化命令 → 读 GC9D01 Read ID 寄存器并打印。
18: 
19: **Tech Stack:** NuttX (ARMv8-M), C, BK7258 QSPI0 controller, GPIO_6 (reset pin, 按
20: `BTdocs/DualScreenAVIPlayer.md` 双屏方案 lcd0 配置), NSH command registration.
21: 
22: ---
23: 
24: ## 背景说明（写给执行者）
25: 
26: 这份计划要移植的硬件通路是：BK7258 AP (CPU1) 通过 **QSPI0** 总线控制一块 **GC9D01**
27: 160x160 单色 LCD 面板。QSPI0 使用 4 根信号线：`CLK=GPIO_22`、`CSN=GPIO_23`、
28: `IO0=GPIO_24`、`IO1=GPIO_25`（这 4 根线走 QSPI controller 自带的专用 IO，不经过通用
29: GPIO 输出驱动），另外面板的 **RESET 引脚**（`GPIO_6`，来自 `BTdocs/DualScreenAVIPlayer.md`
30: 双屏方案 lcd0 配置）需要软件用普通 GPIO output 拉高/拉低/拉高完成硬件复位。
31: 
32: 当前仓库（`board/beken/chips/bk7258/`）里**没有任何 GPIO 驱动、没有任何 QSPI 驱动**，
33: 这两个都要从零写。DMA 驱动也不存在，但本计划刻意避开需要 DMA 的"整帧像素刷新"路径，
34: 只做初始化命令发送（走 QSPI 的 cmd_c 直接命令通道，CPU 轮询完成，不用 DMA）和读 ID
35: 验证（cmd_d 读命令通道），所以不受 DMA 缺失影响。
36: 
37: 已核实的寄存器事实（来自 `bk_avdk_smp` release/v3.1.1 源码，本计划的唯一权威依据）：
38: 
39: - GPIO 寄存器基址：`SOC_AON_GPIO_REG_BASE`，即本仓库 `bk7258_memorymap.h` 里已经定义的
40:   `BK7258_AON_GPIO_BASE = 0x44000400u`。每个引脚占 4 字节（32位配置寄存器），第 N 号
41:   引脚的寄存器地址 = `BK7258_AON_GPIO_BASE + N * 4`。关键位：`bit[1]`=输出电平（1=高，
42:   0=低）、`bit[3]`=输出使能（1=使能输出）。
43:   来源：`bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_struct.h`。
44: - QSPI0 寄存器基址：`SOC_QSPI0_REG_BASE`。本计划新增
45:   `BK7258_QSPI0_BASE`，数值需要在 Task 2 Step 1 从
46:   `bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/sys_reg.h` 或
47:   `bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/common/soc/include/soc.h` 里查出 `SOC_QSPI0_REG_BASE`
48:   的实际数值后再填入（执行者必须先查值，不能假设）。
49: - QSPI 寄存器字（32位对齐，从基址开始按顺序数，每个字占 4 字节偏移）：
50:   - `dev_id`：偏移 `0x00`
51:   - `version_id`：偏移 `0x04`（即字索引1）
52:   - `glb_ctrl`：偏移 `0x08`（字索引2），`bit[0]`=soft_reset，`bit[1]`=bps_clkgate
53:   - `core_status`：偏移 `0x0C`（字索引3）
54:   - reserved0[4]：偏移 `0x10`~`0x1C`（字索引4~7）
55:   - `cmd_a_l`：偏移 `0x20`（字索引8）
56:   - `cmd_a_h`：偏移 `0x24`（字索引9）
57:   - `cmd_a_cfg1`：偏移 `0x28`（字索引10）
58:   - `cmd_a_cfg2`：偏移 `0x2C`（字索引11）
59:   - `cmd_b_l`：偏移 `0x30`（字索引12）
60:   - `cmd_b_h`：偏移 `0x34`（字索引13）
61:   - `cmd_b_cfg1`：偏移 `0x38`（字索引14）
62:   - `cmd_b_cfg2`：偏移 `0x3C`（字索引15）
63: 
64:   本计划只用到 `glb_ctrl`（软复位）、`core_status`（轮询完成状态，具体 bit 需要 Task 2
65:   Step 2 时从 `qspi_struct.h` 剩余部分确认，本文档写作时未读到 `core_status` 的位域
66:   含义和 `cmd_c_*`/`cmd_d_*` 的偏移，执行者必须先读取该文件剩余内容后才能继续写
67:   `bk7258_qspi.c` 的 send/wait/read 函数，见 Task 2 Step 2 的强制前置动作）。
68:   来源：`bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/qspi_struct.h`。

166:     }
167: 
168:     qspi_hal_set_cmd_a_cfg2(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, 0x80008000);
169: 
170:     return BK_OK;
171: }

193: static bk_err_t lcd_qspi_reg_data_convert(qspi_id_t qspi_id, uint8_t *data, uint32_t data_len)
194: {
195:     uint32_t data_buffer[data_len];
196:     uint8_t i, j, data_tmp1;
197:     uint8_t data_tmp2[4];
198: 
199:     bk_qspi_read(qspi_id, data_buffer, data_len * 4);
200:     for (i = 0; i < data_len; i++) {
201:         for (j = 0; j < 4; j++) {
202:             data_tmp1 = (data_buffer[i] >> ((j * 8) + 4)) & 0x1;
203:             data_tmp2[j] = (data_tmp1 << 1) | ((data_buffer[i] >> (j * 8)) & 0x1);
204:         }
205: 
206:         data[i] = (data_tmp2[0] << 6) | (data_tmp2[1] << 4) | (data_tmp2[2] << 2) | (data_tmp2[3]);
207:     }
208: 
209:     return BK_OK;
210: }

212: static bk_err_t lcd_qspi_refresh_by_line_lcd_head_config(qspi_id_t qspi_id, const lcd_device_t *device)
213: {
214:     uint8_t *cmd = NULL;
215:     uint32_t head_cmd[4];
216:     uint8_t i;
217: 
218:     cmd = device->qspi->pixel_write_config.cmd;
219:     for (i = 0; i < device->qspi->pixel_write_config.cmd_len; i++) {
220:         if (0 == cmd[i]) {
221:             head_cmd[i] = 0x0;
222:             continue;
223:         } else {
224:             uint8_t cmd_temp = cmd[i];
225:             cmd_temp = ((cmd_temp >> 4) & 0x0F) | ((cmd_temp << 4) & 0xF0);
226:             cmd_temp = ((cmd_temp >> 2) & 0x33) | ((cmd_temp << 2) & 0xCC);
227:             cmd_temp = ((cmd_temp >> 1) & 0x55) | ((cmd_temp << 1) & 0xAA);
228: 
229:             head_cmd[i] = ((cmd_temp << 21) & 0x10000000) | ((cmd_temp << 18) & 0x01000000) |
230:                         ((cmd_temp << 15) & 0x00100000) | ((cmd_temp << 12) & 0x00010000) |
231:                         ((cmd_temp << 9) & 0x00001000) | ((cmd_temp << 6) & 0x00000100) |
232:                         ((cmd_temp << 3) & 0x00000010) | (cmd_temp & 0x00000001);
233:         }
234:     }
235: 
236:     qspi_hal_set_lcd_head_cmd0(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, head_cmd[0]);
237:     qspi_hal_set_lcd_head_cmd1(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, head_cmd[1]);
238:     qspi_hal_set_lcd_head_cmd2(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, head_cmd[2]);
239:     qspi_hal_set_lcd_head_cmd3(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, head_cmd[3]);
240:     qspi_hal_set_lcd_head_resolution(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, device->qspi->refresh_config.line_len * 2, device->height);
241: 
242:     qspi_hal_enable_lcd_head_selection_without_ram(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal);
243:     qspi_hal_set_lcd_head_len(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, 0x20);
244:     qspi_hal_set_lcd_head_dly(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, (device->qspi->clk >> 1) + 6);
245: 
246:     return BK_OK;
247: }

255:     qspi_hal_set_cmd_d_h(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, (regist_addr << 16 | device->qspi->reg_read_cmd) & 0xFF00FF);

261:     qspi_hal_set_cmd_d_dummy_mode(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, device->qspi->reg_read_config.dummy_mode);

263:     qspi_hal_cmd_d_start(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal);
264:     qspi_hal_wait_cmd_done(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal);

268:     return BK_OK;

271: bk_err_t bk_lcd_qspi_send_cmd(qspi_id_t qspi_id, uint8_t write_cmd, uint8_t cmd, const uint8_t *data, uint8_t data_len)
272: {
273:     qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_l(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, 0);
274:     qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_h(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, 0);
275:     qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_cfg1(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, 0);
276:     qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_cfg2(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, 0);
277: 
278:     if (data_len == 0) {
279:         qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_h(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, (cmd << 16 | write_cmd) & 0xFF00FF);
280:     } else if (data_len > 0 && data_len <= 4) {
281:         uint32_t value = 0;
282:         for (uint8_t i = 0; i < data_len; i++) {
283:             value = value | (data[i] << (i * 8));
284:         }
285:         qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_l(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, value);
286:         qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_h(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, (cmd << 16 | write_cmd) & 0xFF00FF);
287:     } else if (data_len > 4 && data_len != 0xFF) {
288:         qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_h(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, (cmd << 16 | write_cmd) & 0xFF00FF);
289:         qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_cfg1(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, 0x300);
290:         qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_cfg2(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, data_len << 2);
291:         bk_qspi_write(qspi_id, data, data_len);
292:         qspi_hal_cmd_c_start(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal);
293:         qspi_hal_wait_cmd_done(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal);
294:         qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_cfg1(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, 0);
295:         qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_cfg2(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, 0);
296:         return BK_OK;
297:     }
298: 
299:     qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_cfg1(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, 0x3 << ((data_len + 4) * 2));
300:     qspi_hal_cmd_c_start(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal);
301:     qspi_hal_wait_cmd_done(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal);
302: 
303:     return BK_OK;
304: }

306: bk_err_t bk_lcd_qspi_quad_write_start(qspi_id_t qspi_id, lcd_qspi_write_config_t reg_config, bool addr_is_4wire)
307: {
308:     uint32_t cmd_c_h = 0;
309: 
310:     qspi_hal_force_spi_cs_low_enable(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal);
311: 
312:     qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_h(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, 0);
313: 
314:     for (uint8_t i = 0; i < reg_config.cmd_len; i++) {
315:         cmd_c_h = qspi_hal_get_cmd_c_h(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal);
316:         cmd_c_h |= ((reg_config.cmd[i]) << i * 8);
317:         qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_h(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, cmd_c_h);
318:     }
319: 
320:     if (addr_is_4wire) {
321:         qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_cfg1(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, 0x3A8);
322:     } else {
323:         qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_cfg1(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, 0x300);
324:     }
325:     qspi_hal_cmd_c_start(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal);
326:     qspi_hal_wait_cmd_done(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal);
327: 
328:     qspi_hal_io_cpu_mem_select(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal, 1);
329:     qspi_hal_disable_cmd_sck_enable(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal);
330: 
331:     return BK_OK;
332: }

444:     dma_config.src.start_addr = (uint32_t)data;
445:     dma_config.src.end_addr = (uint32_t)(data + data_len);
446: 
447:     dma_config.dst.dev = DMA_DEV_DTCM;
448:     dma_config.dst.width = DMA_DATA_WIDTH_32BITS;

451:     dma_config.dst.start_addr = s_qspi_disp[qspi_id].qspi_data;

478: bk_err_t bk_lcd_qspi_init(qspi_id_t qspi_id, const lcd_device_t *device, uint8_t reset_pin)
479: {
480:     bk_err_t ret = BK_OK;
481: 
482:     if (device == NULL) {
483:         LCD_QSPI_LOGE("lcd qspi device not found\r\n");
484:         return BK_FAIL;
485:     }
486: 
487:     if (s_qspi_disp[qspi_id].lcd_qspi_is_init) {
488:         LCD_QSPI_LOGE("lcd qspi init already complete\r\n");
489:         return BK_OK;
490:     }
491: 
492:     lcd_qspi_dma_init(qspi_id);
493: 
494:     qspi_hal_disable_soft_reset(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal);
495:     bk_delay_us(10);
496:     qspi_hal_enable_soft_reset(&s_lcd_qspi[qspi_id].hal);
497: 
498:     lcd_qspi_hardware_reset(reset_pin);
499: 
500:     ret = lcd_qspi_driver_init(qspi_id, device->qspi->clk);
501:     if (ret != BK_OK) {
502:         LCD_QSPI_LOGE("lcd qspi driver init failed!\r\n");
503:         return ret;
504:     }
505: 
506:     if (device->qspi->refresh_method == LCD_QSPI_REFRESH_BY_LINE) {
507:         lcd_qspi_refresh_by_line_lcd_head_config(qspi_id, device);
508:     } else {
509:         lcd_display_area_t disp_area = {0};
510:         disp_area.x_start = 0;
511:         disp_area.y_start = 0;
512:         disp_area.x_end = device->width - 1;
513:         disp_area.y_end = device->height - 1;
514:         lcd_qspi_disp_area_config(qspi_id, device, &disp_area);
515:     }
516: 
517:     if (device->qspi->init_cmd != NULL) {
518:         const lcd_qspi_init_cmd_t *init = device->qspi->init_cmd;
519:         for (uint32_t i = 0; i < device->qspi->device_init_cmd_len; i++) {
520:             if (init->data_len == 0xff) {
521:                 rtos_delay_milliseconds(init->data[0]);
522:             } else {
523:                 bk_lcd_qspi_send_cmd(qspi_id, device->qspi->reg_write_cmd, init->cmd, init->data, init->data_len);
524:             }
525:             init++;
526:         }
527:     } else {
528:         LCD_QSPI_LOGE("lcd qspi device don't init\r\n");
529:         return BK_FAIL;
530:     }
531: 
532:     s_qspi_disp[qspi_id].lcd_qspi_is_init = true;
533: 
534:     return BK_OK;
535: }

537: bk_err_t bk_lcd_qspi_deinit(qspi_id_t qspi_id, uint8_t reset_pin)
538: {
539:     if (s_qspi_disp[qspi_id].lcd_qspi_is_init == false) {
540:         LCD_QSPI_LOGE("lcd qspi deinit already complete\r\n");
541:         return BK_OK;
542:     }
543: 
544:     lcd_qspi_dma_deinit(qspi_id);
545: 
546:     BK_LOG_ON_ERR(bk_qspi_deinit(qspi_id));
547: 
548:     gpio_dev_unmap(reset_pin);

555: bk_err_t bk_lcd_qspi_wait_display_complete(qspi_id_t qspi_id, const lcd_device_t *device)

559:     if (s_qspi_disp[qspi_id].dma_sema) {

579: bk_err_t bk_lcd_qspi_frame_display(qspi_id_t qspi_id, const lcd_device_t *device, uint32_t *data, uint32_t data_len)
580: {
581:     if (data_len <= 0x10000) {
582:         s_qspi_disp[qspi_id].dma_is_repeat_mode = false;
583:         lcd_qspi_dma_single_mode_config(qspi_id, s_qspi_disp[qspi_id].dma_id, data, data_len);
584:     } else {
585:         s_qspi_disp[qspi_id].dma_is_repeat_mode = true;
586:         lcd_qspi_dma_repeat_mode_config(qspi_id, s_qspi_disp[qspi_id].dma_id, data, data_len);
587:     }
588: 
589:     if (device->qspi->refresh_method == LCD_QSPI_REFRESH_BY_LINE) {

305: #define QSPI_CLK_DIV_INTERNAL_DEFAULT   (2)
306: #define QSPI_SCK_MAX_HZ                 (80000000u)
307: /* clk_div is an 8-bit field; bound the search to a sane range. */
308: #define QSPI_CLK_DIV_SEARCH_MAX         (15u)
309: /* Hardware requires the source divider (src_clk_div) to be at least 4. */
310: #define QSPI_SRC_CLK_DIV_MIN            (4u)
311: 
312: /* Second-stage divider factor for clk_div: clk_div == 0 bypasses the stage
313:  * (divide by 1), otherwise the stage divides by (2 * clk_div). */
314: static inline uint32_t qspi_clk_div_factor(uint32_t clk_div)
315: {
316: 	return (clk_div == 0u) ? 1u : (2u * clk_div);
317: }
318: 
319: /* SCK on 7258 is derived from the source clock through two divider stages:
320:  *   stage 1: (1 + src_clk_div)
321:  *   stage 2: clk_div == 0 -> bypass (÷1), else (2 * clk_div)
322:  * so SCK = src_clk / ((1 + src_clk_div) * (clk_div ? 2 * clk_div : 1)).
323:  * Pick the src_clk/src_clk_div/clk_div combination whose frequency is closest
324:  * to clk_hz without exceeding QSPI_SCK_MAX_HZ. Hardware requires
325:  * src_clk_div >= QSPI_SRC_CLK_DIV_MIN. */
326: static void qspi_calc_clock_config(qspi_config_t *config, uint32_t clk_hz)
327: {
328: 	static const struct {
329: 		uint32_t hz;
330: 		qspi_src_clk_t sel;
331: 	} src_tbl[] = {
332: 		{ 480000000u, QSPI_SCLK_480M },
333: 		{ 320000000u, QSPI_SCLK_320M },
334: 	};
335: 	uint32_t best_diff = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
336: 
337: 	/* fallback default = 480M / ((1 + 4) * (2 * 2)) = 24MHz */
338: 	config->src_clk = QSPI_SCLK_480M;
339: 	config->src_clk_div = 4;
340: 	config->clk_div = QSPI_CLK_DIV_INTERNAL_DEFAULT;
341: 
342: 	for (uint32_t s = 0; s < (sizeof(src_tbl) / sizeof(src_tbl[0])); s++) {
343: 		for (uint32_t sd = QSPI_SRC_CLK_DIV_MIN; sd <= 15; sd++) {
344: 			for (uint32_t cd = 0; cd <= QSPI_CLK_DIV_SEARCH_MAX; cd++) {
345: 				uint32_t f = src_tbl[s].hz / ((1u + sd) * qspi_clk_div_factor(cd));
346: 				if (f > QSPI_SCK_MAX_HZ) {
347: 					continue;
348: 				}
349: 				uint32_t diff = (f > clk_hz) ? (f - clk_hz) : (clk_hz - f);
350: 				if (diff < best_diff) {
351: 					best_diff = diff;
352: 					config->src_clk = src_tbl[s].sel;
353: 					config->src_clk_div = sd;
354: 					config->clk_div = cd;
355: 				}
356: 			}
357: 		}
358: 	}
359: }

38: /* Program the address bytes (MSB first) into cmd2.. of the send (cmd_c) path. */
39: static bk_err_t qspi_hal_set_send_addr(qspi_hal_t *hal, uint32_t addr, uint32_t addr_len)
40: {
41: 	if (addr_len == 0) {
42: 		return BK_OK;
43: 	}
44: 	if (addr_len > 4) {
45: 		return BK_FAIL;
46: 	}
47: 
48: 	uint32_t shift = (addr_len - 1) * 8;
49: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_c_cmd2(hal->hw, (addr >> shift) & QSPI_F_CMD_VALUE_M);
50: 	if (addr_len > 1) {
51: 		shift -= 8;
52: 		qspi_ll_set_cmd_c_cmd3(hal->hw, (addr >> shift) & QSPI_F_CMD_VALUE_M);
53: 	}
54: 	if (addr_len > 2) {
55: 		shift -= 8;
56: 		qspi_ll_set_cmd_c_cmd4(hal->hw, (addr >> shift) & QSPI_F_CMD_VALUE_M);
57: 	}
58: 	if (addr_len > 3) {
59: 		qspi_ll_set_cmd_c_cmd5(hal->hw, addr & QSPI_F_CMD_VALUE_M);
60: 	}
61: 	return BK_OK;
62: }

64: /* Set the per-byte line config for the send address; unused slots are disabled
65:  * so the controller stops the command phase right after the address. */
66: static bk_err_t qspi_hal_set_send_addr_line(qspi_hal_t *hal, qspi_wire_mode_t wire_mode, uint32_t addr_len)
67: {
68: 	if (addr_len > 4) {
69: 		return BK_FAIL;
70: 	}
71: 
72: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_c_cmd2_line(hal->hw, addr_len > 0 ? wire_mode : QSPI_CMD_DISABLE);
73: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_c_cmd3_line(hal->hw, addr_len > 1 ? wire_mode : QSPI_CMD_DISABLE);
74: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_c_cmd4_line(hal->hw, addr_len > 2 ? wire_mode : QSPI_CMD_DISABLE);
75: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_c_cmd5_line(hal->hw, addr_len > 3 ? wire_mode : QSPI_CMD_DISABLE);
76: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_c_cmd6_line(hal->hw, QSPI_CMD_DISABLE);
77: 	return BK_OK;
78: }

80: /* Program the address bytes (MSB first) into cmd2.. of the recv (cmd_d) path. */
81: static bk_err_t qspi_hal_set_recv_addr(qspi_hal_t *hal, uint32_t addr, uint32_t addr_len)
82: {
83: 	if (addr_len == 0) {
84: 		return BK_OK;
85: 	}
86: 	if (addr_len > 4) {
87: 		return BK_FAIL;
88: 	}
89: 
90: 	uint32_t shift = (addr_len - 1) * 8;
91: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd2(hal->hw, (addr >> shift) & QSPI_F_CMD_VALUE_M);
92: 	if (addr_len > 1) {
93: 		shift -= 8;
94: 		qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd3(hal->hw, (addr >> shift) & QSPI_F_CMD_VALUE_M);
95: 	}
96: 	if (addr_len > 2) {
97: 		shift -= 8;
98: 		qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd4(hal->hw, (addr >> shift) & QSPI_F_CMD_VALUE_M);
99: 	}
100: 	if (addr_len > 3) {
101: 		qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd5(hal->hw, addr & QSPI_F_CMD_VALUE_M);
102: 	}
103: 	return BK_OK;
104: }
105: 
106: /* Set the per-byte line config for the recv address; unused slots are disabled. */
107: static bk_err_t qspi_hal_set_recv_addr_line(qspi_hal_t *hal, qspi_wire_mode_t wire_mode, uint32_t addr_len)
108: {
109: 	if (addr_len > 4) {
110: 		return BK_FAIL;
111: 	}
112: 
113: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd2_line(hal->hw, addr_len > 0 ? wire_mode : QSPI_CMD_DISABLE);
114: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd3_line(hal->hw, addr_len > 1 ? wire_mode : QSPI_CMD_DISABLE);
115: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd4_line(hal->hw, addr_len > 2 ? wire_mode : QSPI_CMD_DISABLE);
116: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd5_line(hal->hw, addr_len > 3 ? wire_mode : QSPI_CMD_DISABLE);
117: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd6_line(hal->hw, QSPI_CMD_DISABLE);
118: 	return BK_OK;
119: }
120: 
121: /* Set a single recv command byte (value + line) at the given cmd slot index. */
122: static bk_err_t qspi_hal_set_recv_cmd_byte(qspi_hal_t *hal, uint32_t index, uint8_t value, qspi_wire_mode_t wire_mode)
123: {
124: 	switch (index) {
125: 	case 2: qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd2(hal->hw, value); qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd2_line(hal->hw, wire_mode); break;
126: 	case 3: qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd3(hal->hw, value); qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd3_line(hal->hw, wire_mode); break;
127: 	case 4: qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd4(hal->hw, value); qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd4_line(hal->hw, wire_mode); break;
128: 	case 5: qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd5(hal->hw, value); qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd5_line(hal->hw, wire_mode); break;
129: 	case 6: qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd6(hal->hw, value); qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd6_line(hal->hw, wire_mode); break;
130: 	case 7: qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd7(hal->hw, value); qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd7_line(hal->hw, wire_mode); break;
131: 	case 8: qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd8(hal->hw, value); qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd8_line(hal->hw, wire_mode); break;
132: 	default: return BK_FAIL;
133: 	}
134: 	return BK_OK;
135: }
136: 
137: /*
138:  * Issue an indirect write command (cmd_c). The opcode is always single-wire,
139:  * the address follows at cmd->addr_wire_mode; write data goes through the
140:  * FIFO-fed data phase.
141:  */
142: static bk_err_t qspi_hal_send_command(qspi_hal_t *hal, const qspi_cmd_t *cmd)
143: {
144: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_c_l(hal->hw, 0);
145: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_c_h(hal->hw, 0);
146: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_c_cfg1(hal->hw, 0);
147: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_c_cfg2(hal->hw, 0);
148: 
149: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_c_cmd1(hal->hw, cmd->cmd);
150: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_c_cmd1_line(hal->hw, QSPI_1WIRE);
151: 	BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(qspi_hal_set_send_addr(hal, cmd->addr, cmd->addr_len));
152: 	BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(qspi_hal_set_send_addr_line(hal, cmd->addr_wire_mode, cmd->addr_len));
153: 
154: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_c_data_length(hal->hw, cmd->data_len);
155: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_c_data_line(hal->hw, cmd->data_wire_mode);
156: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_c_dummy_clock(hal->hw, cmd->dummy_cycle);
157: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_c_dummy_mode(hal->hw, cmd->dummy_mode);
158: 	qspi_ll_cmd_c_start(hal->hw);
159: 	qspi_ll_wait_cmd_done(hal->hw);
160: 	return BK_OK;
161: }
162: 
163: /*
164:  * Issue an indirect read command (cmd_d). When the address itself is clocked on
165:  * four wires (NOR quad I/O read), one extra 4-wire mode byte is appended after
166:  * the address (cfg1 == 0xea8 for a 3-byte-address quad read).
167:  */
168: static bk_err_t qspi_hal_recv_command(qspi_hal_t *hal, const qspi_cmd_t *cmd)
169: {
170: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_l(hal->hw, 0);
171: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_h(hal->hw, 0);
172: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cfg1(hal->hw, 0);
173: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cfg2(hal->hw, 0);
174: 
175: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd1(hal->hw, cmd->cmd);
176: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_cmd1_line(hal->hw, QSPI_1WIRE);
177: 	BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(qspi_hal_set_recv_addr(hal, cmd->addr, cmd->addr_len));
178: 	BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(qspi_hal_set_recv_addr_line(hal, cmd->addr_wire_mode, cmd->addr_len));
179: 
180: 	if (cmd->addr_wire_mode == QSPI_4WIRE && cmd->addr_len > 0) {
181: 		BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(qspi_hal_set_recv_cmd_byte(hal, 2 + cmd->addr_len, 0, QSPI_4WIRE));
182: 	}
183: 
184: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_data_length(hal->hw, cmd->data_len);
185: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_data_line(hal->hw, cmd->data_wire_mode);
186: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_dummy_clock(hal->hw, cmd->dummy_cycle);
187: 	qspi_ll_set_cmd_d_dummy_mode(hal->hw, cmd->dummy_mode);
188: 	qspi_ll_cmd_d_start(hal->hw);
189: 	qspi_ll_wait_cmd_done(hal->hw);
190: 	return BK_OK;
191: }
192: 
193: bk_err_t qspi_hal_command(qspi_hal_t *hal, const qspi_cmd_t *cmd)
194: {
195: 	s_current_sw_op = cmd->op;
196: 
197: 	/* NOR indirect flash commands are built here via the generic send/recv
198: 	 * path; PSRAM and memory-mapped commands still go through qspi_ll. */
199: 	if (cmd->device == QSPI_FLASH && cmd->work_mode != MEMORY_MAPPED_MODE) {
200: 		if (cmd->op == QSPI_WRITE) {
201: 			return qspi_hal_send_command(hal, cmd);
202: 		} else if (cmd->op == QSPI_READ) {
203: 			return qspi_hal_recv_command(hal, cmd);
204: 		}
205: 		return BK_FAIL;
206: 	}
207: 
208: 	qspi_ll_init_command(hal->hw, cmd);
209: 	return BK_OK;
210: }

On this board, however, the schematic notes route only CLK/CS/D0/D1 to QSPI1, so a QSPI command-channel shim can emulate the required 4-wire SPI transaction—but it must encode only the GC9D01 command/data bytes and terminate the active slots correctly. I’m collecting the exact vendor SPI timing/power sequence for the final minimal diff.

text:
## Conclusion

The timeout is caused by the **QSPI1 controller not being placed in an operational state**, not by GC9D01 failing to acknowledge `0xfe`.

Two concrete initialization defects are present in `bk7258_qspi.c`:

1. **The soft-reset sequence is backwards.**  
   The target leaves `QSPI1_GLB_CTRL.soft_reset` at `0`, while the vendor LCD-over-QSPI path leaves it at `1`.

2. **`QSPI_CONFIG.qspi_en` is never set.**  
   The vendor’s common QSPI initialization explicitly sets `CONFIG.bit0 = 1`; the target never accesses `CONFIG` at offset `0x60`.

The omitted **AHBP QSPI1 power-domain vote** can independently produce the same dead-controller symptom if the domain is not already held on by another AP/CP user. Enabling only `SYS_DEVCLK_EN.bit21` is not equivalent to powering the AHBP domain.

Wrong panel power or panel wiring cannot, by itself, explain `cmd_start_done` never setting. QSPI command completion is controller-local; the GC9D01 does not return an acknowledgment for command `0xfe`.

No files were modified.

---

## Primary evidence

### 1. Target leaves QSPI in the opposite reset state

Target code:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_qspi.c:172-175`

```c
putreg32(QSPI_GLB_CTRL_SOFT_RESET, QSPI_GLB_CTRL);
up_udelay(10);
putreg32(0, QSPI_GLB_CTRL);
```

Vendor code does the reverse:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/lcd/lcd_spi_driver.c:372-374`

```c
qspi_hal_disable_soft_reset(...);  /* writes 0 */
bk_delay_us(10);
qspi_hal_enable_soft_reset(...);   /* writes 1 */
```

The helper definitions confirm those literal values:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/qspi_ll.h:466-475`

```c
static inline void qspi_ll_enable_soft_reset(qspi_hw_t *hw)
{
    hw->glb_ctrl.soft_reset = 1;
}

static inline void qspi_ll_disable_soft_reset(qspi_hw_t *hw)
{
    hw->glb_ctrl.soft_reset = 0;
}
```

Therefore, regardless of the misleading field name, the vendor-tested operational final value is:

```text
QSPI1 base + 0x08, bit0 = 1
```

The target leaves it at zero immediately before issuing `0xfe`.

---

### 2. Target never sets `QSPI_CONFIG.qspi_en`

The register is documented at QSPI word `0x18`, byte offset `0x60`:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/qspi_struct.h:258-280`

```c
/* REG_0x18 */
union {
    struct {
        uint32_t qspi_en:           1;  /* bit0 */
        uint32_t cpol:              1;
        uint32_t cpha:              1;
        uint32_t io2_io3_mode:      1;  /* bit3 */
        ...
    };
    uint32_t v;
} config;
```

Vendor common initialization sets both bit 0 and bit 3:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/qspi_ll.h:675-679`

```c
static inline void qspi_ll_init_common(qspi_hw_t *hw)
{
    qspi_ll_enable(hw);              /* CONFIG.bit0 = 1 */
    qspi_ll_enable_io2_io3_mode(hw); /* CONFIG.bit3 = 1 */
}
```

That common initialization is called by:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/qspi/qspi_driver.c:221-228`

The target driver defines no register at offset `0x60` and never enables the QSPI core.

For QSPI1:

```text
QSPI1_CONFIG = 0x46060000 + 0x60 = 0x46060060
Required minimum: bit0 = 1
Vendor-compatible value: bit0 | bit3 = 0x00000009
```

`bit3` is not inherently required for this three-signal, one-wire command use, but matching the vendor common initialization is safe. `bit0` is essential.

---

### 3. Vendor explicitly powers the AHBP/QSPI1 domain

Vendor QSPI1 initialization begins with:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/qspi/qspi_driver.c:274-287`

```c
} else if (id == QSPI_ID_1) {
    bk_pm_module_vote_power_ctrl(
        PM_POWER_SUB_MODULE_NAME_AHBP_QSPI1,
        PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON);
}

qspi_id_init_common(id);
```

The target only sets the leaf module clock:

```c
modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_DEVCLK_EN, 0,
            BK7258_QSPI1_MODULE_CLK_EN);
```

That is:

```text
SYSCTRL 0x44010030 bit21 = QSPI1 leaf clock gate
```

It is not the AHBP power-domain vote.

The numeric vendor power vote is:

```text
PM_POWER_CTRL_CMD                         = 0x01
POWER_MODULE_NAME_AHBP                    = 5
PM_MODULE_SUB_POWER_DOMAIN_MAX            = 20
POWER_SUB_MODULE_NAME_AHBP_QSPI1          = 5*20 + 4 = 104
PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON                  = 0
```

Thus the AP-to-CP PWC operation is conceptually:

```text
command = 0x01
param1  = 104       /* AHBP_QSPI1 */
param2  = 0         /* ON */
param3  = 0
```

The target already has a PWC transport in:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c`

but its generic send routine is static and it currently has special response handling only for PSRAM. A proper QSPI power vote should be exposed through that framework and should wait for the CP’s `PM_POWER_CTRL_CMD` response, not merely for the mailbox transport ACK.

If runtime inspection proves the AHBP domain is already on and held by another module, this vote is not the immediate blocker. It should nevertheless be made explicit to match the vendor initialization and survive low-power transitions.

---

## Clock details

The current target enables only the QSPI1 leaf gate. It does not program the source selector or source divider used by the vendor.

QSPI1 clock source/divider is in SYSCTRL register word `0x0a`:

```text
Address: 0x44010000 + 0x28 = 0x44010028
bits  6:9  ckdiv_qspi1
bit     10 cksel_qspi1
```

Vendor’s GC9D01 descriptor requests 60 MHz:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_peripheral/src/lcd/spi/lcd_spi_gc9d01.c:73-79`

```c
.clk = LCD_QSPI_60M
```

Vendor’s QSPI-backed SPI initialization chooses:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/lcd/lcd_spi_driver.c:330-334`

```c
src_clk = QSPI_SCLK_480M;
src_clk_div = 7;
```

This gives:

```text
480 MHz / (1 + 7) = 60 MHz
```

The selector values are:

```text
QSPI_CLK_320M = 0
QSPI_CLK_480M = 1
```

Therefore the deterministic 60 MHz SYSCTRL setting is:

```c
#define BK7258_SYS_QSPI1_CLK_CFG   0x44010028u
#define QSPI1_CLK_CFG_MASK         (0x1fu << 6)  /* bits 6..10 */
#define QSPI1_CLK_60M_VALUE        ((7u << 6) | (1u << 10))
                                           /* = 0x5c0 */
```

Then:

```c
modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_QSPI1_CLK_CFG,
            QSPI1_CLK_CFG_MASK,
            QSPI1_CLK_60M_VALUE);

modifyreg32(0x44010030u, 0, 1u << 21);
```

The QSPI controller’s second-stage divider is `CONFIG.bits8:15`. Vendor’s zero-initialized QSPI configuration leaves this at zero, meaning bypass/divide-by-one for this LCD path.

---

## Pinmux and schematic findings

The QSPI1 bus selection itself is correct, but the current use of GPIO5 is not.

Schematic:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/博通网页文档/AIDK_AI玩具开发板_原理图.pdf`

The chip table shows:

```text
QFN pin 36: P2 / 1QSCK
QFN pin 35: P3 / 1QCS
QFN pin 34: P4 / 1QIO0
QFN pin 33: P5 / 1QIO1
QFN pin 65: P45, net LCD_RST
```

The single-panel connector shows:

```text
LCD_QSPI_CLK -> panel SCL
LCD_QSPI_CS  -> panel CS
LCD_QSPI_D0  -> panel SDA
LCD_QSPI_D1  -> panel D/C
LCD_RST      -> panel RESET
```

The vendor pin map confirms function index 6:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h:30-35`

```text
GPIO2 function 6 = QSPI1_CLK
GPIO3 function 6 = QSPI1_CSN
GPIO4 function 6 = QSPI1_IO0
GPIO5 function 6 = QSPI1_IO1
```

### Correct pin ownership for this GC9D01

Because the physical panel assigns `LCD_QSPI_D1` to **D/C**, GPIO5 must not remain owned by QSPI1_IO1 for initialization commands.

Use:

```text
GPIO2: function 6, QSPI1_CLK
GPIO3: function 6, QSPI1_CSN
GPIO4: function 6, QSPI1_IO0/MOSI
GPIO5: ordinary GPIO output, GC9D01 D/C
GPIO45: ordinary GPIO output, GC9D01 RESET
```

The target currently maps all four GPIO2–5 to QSPI1:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_qspi.c:167-170`

That is inappropriate for this particular panel wiring. It will not cause the controller-local timeout, but it will prevent valid GC9D01 command/data signaling after the controller timeout is fixed.

The source comments claiming the schematic’s D0/D1 labels are arbitrary and that GPIO5’s “real role” must be QSPI1_IO1 are incorrect in this context: the panel connector explicitly makes D1 the GC9D01 D/C signal.

### Recommended electrical GPIO settings

Vendor QSPI setup also applies:

- Pull-up on CS.
- Pull-up on IO0.
- Drive capacity `3` on CLK, CS and IO0.
- D/C initially high as an ordinary GPIO.

The target pinmux helper currently clears pull configuration and does not set drive capacity. This is not the cause of an internal timeout, but should be matched for reliable 60 MHz operation.

GPIO configuration addresses are:

```text
GPIO2  0x44000408
GPIO3  0x4400040c
GPIO4  0x44000410
GPIO5  0x44000414
GPIO45 0x440004b4
GPIO52 0x440004d0
```

Drive capacity is `bits8:9`; capacity 3 means setting both bits.

---

## GC9D01 command framing is also currently wrong

The vendor GC9D01 is explicitly described as an SPI panel:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_peripheral/src/lcd/spi/lcd_spi_gc9d01.c:81-89`

```c
.type = LCD_TYPE_SPI,
.spi = &lcd_spi_gc9d01_config,
```

The vendor SPI path toggles D/C and sends command and data separately:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/lcd/lcd_spi_driver.c:480-506`

```c
/* Command */
bk_gpio_set_output_low(dc_pin);
lcd_spi_send_data_with_qspi_indirect_mode(id, &cmd, 1);

/* Payload */
bk_gpio_set_output_high(dc_pin);
lcd_spi_send_data_with_qspi_indirect_mode(id, data, data_len);
```

For a one-byte command through QSPI `cmd_c`, vendor uses:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/lcd/lcd_spi_driver.c:390-406`

```c
qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_h(..., value);
qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_cfg1(..., 0x3 << (data_len * 2));
qspi_hal_cmd_c_start(...);
```

Thus for the first `0xfe` byte:

```text
CMD_C_H    = 0x000000fe
CMD_C_CFG1 = 0x0000000c  /* 3 << 2: disable slot 2 */
```

The target instead does:

```text
CMD_C_H    = 0x000000fe
CMD_C_CFG1 = 0
```

`CMD_C_CFG1=0` means all command slots are configured as one-wire bytes; it does not mean “one-byte command.” It can clock trailing zero bytes.

The target also places payload bytes into `CMD_C_L`, slots 5–8, while leaving slots 2–4 enabled as zeros. That is not the vendor GC9D01 SPI protocol.

---

## Panel power

The generic vendor example enables an external LCD LDO on GPIO13:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/spi_lcd_example/ap/ap_main.c:21,87`

However, that GPIO assignment must not be copied to this board.

The actual board schematic shows:

```text
Panel VDD  -> LDO_3V3
Panel LEDA -> LDO_3V3
LDO_3V3 generated by U3
U3 enable net LDO33_EN -> P52 / GPIO52
```

GPIO13 is not the LCD LDO enable on this PCB.

Therefore:

- Ensure GPIO52 is driven high before panel reset if CP/boot firmware has not already enabled `LDO33_EN`.
- Wait for the 3.3 V rail to settle.
- Then reset GPIO45 low and high.
- Backlight control `LCD_BL_PWM` is on P25 and is unrelated to QSPI command completion.

A dead panel rail still does **not** explain a missing QSPI `cmd_start_done`; it only explains why correctly transmitted commands have no visible effect.

### B. Minimum protocol correction needed after the timeout is gone

Implement a one-to-four-byte helper that packs bytes into `CMD_C_H` and terminates the next slot:

```c
static bool qspi_send_bytes(const uint8_t *bytes, uint8_t len)
{
    uint32_t value = 0;

    for (uint8_t i = 0; i < len; i++)
        value |= (uint32_t)bytes[i] << (8u * i);

    putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_C_L);
    putreg32(value, QSPI_CMD_C_H);
    putreg32(3u << (len * 2u), QSPI_CMD_C_CFG1);
    putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_C_CFG2);
    modifyreg32(QSPI_CMD_C_CFG2, 0, QSPI_CMD_START_BIT);

    return bk7258_qspi0_wait_done();
}
```

## Register checklist for hardware validation

Immediately before starting `0xfe`, inspect:

```text
0x44010028 & 0x000007c0 = 0x000005c0  QSPI1 source=480M, divider=7
0x44010030 & 0x00200000 = 0x00200000  QSPI1 leaf clock enabled

0x46060008 & 0x1        = 1           vendor operational reset state
0x46060060 & 0x1        = 1           QSPI enabled

0x46060044              = 0x000000fe
0x46060048              = 0x0000000c
0x4606004c bit0         transitions to 1
0x46060070 bit2         becomes 1 on completion
0x46060070 bit4         should remain 0; bit4 is cmd_start_fail
```

On a logic analyzer:

```text
P2/GPIO2: QSPI1 clock pulses
P3/GPIO3: CS goes low during the transfer
P4/GPIO4: transmits 0xfe, MSB first
P5/GPIO5: held low for the command; high for payload transfers
P45: high after reset
P52: high and LDO_3V3 present, unless CP already controls the rail
```

If `STATUS.bit2` still remains zero with `GLB_CTRL.bit0=1` and `CONFIG.bit0=1`, the next check is the missing AHBP power vote—not the LCD wiring.
